characterization_methods.key_findings: Deformation substructure of the ~30% Al alloy consists of superdislocations composed of two (1/2)111 partials, many straight near-screw dislocations, and many edge dislocation dipoles and loops; parallel pairs are dipole pairs; reactions produce stepped structures; APBII residual-contrast fringes traverse the field.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Dislocations imaged in Bright Field and Weak Beam modes; planar (shear or thermal) faults observed in various dark field modes; Burgers vectors identified using standard procedures of imaging with a variety of g vectors, generally in Bright Field mode where dislocation invisibility is more closely achieved.
characterization_methods.purpose: Examine dislocation structures produced by room-temperature straining and identify dislocation Burgers vectors for the Fe–30% Al base alloy.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: 25% nitric acid in methanol mixture, about 20 V, −30 °C; foils cut from the centre of the deformed samples perpendicular to the stress axis with a diamond saw.
characterization_methods.purpose: Prepare electron-transparent thin foils from the deformed samples for dislocation-structure examination.

defect_interactions.interaction_type: APB fault trailing / partial separation within superdislocations
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: For Fe–30% Al the APBI fault energy is sufficiently high that the separation of the partials constituting the superdislocation is small; the parallel image pairs all correspond to short or long dipole dislocation pairs rather than widely separated partials.

In Fe–30% Al, dislocation pairs observed (Figs. 15, 16) are the result of dislocation reactions and do not correspond to the partials of the glissile superdislocations; reactions produce stepped structures.

defect_interactions.interaction_type: DO3 order destruction by glide of (1/2)111 partial pairs leaving APBII faults
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Fringes traversing the imaged area are due to residual contrast of APBII fringes produced during deformation of this weakly DO3-ordered material, since the pairs of (1/2)111 partials destroy this order during movement.

interfaces.slip_behavior: Deformation of the ~30% Al alloy occurs by movement of superdislocations composed of two (1/2)111 partials (perfect superdislocations for the B2 lattice, imperfect for the DO3 lattice, hence trailing APBII faults); dislocations are predominantly straight and in near-screw orientations.

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: Effect of ~0.1 at.% B addition on flow stress and work hardening rate of Fe–30% Al: only a slight increase in flow stress relative to the B-free samples, with little consistent change in the work hardening rate

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Fe–Al base alloys (including the 30% Al + 0.1% B alloy) prepared by standard induction melting in an alumina crucible under inert gas.

processing_steps.method: drop casting into cylindrical copper mould
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Drop cast into a 25 mm diameter cylindrical copper mould to produce samples with grain size of the order of 0.25 mm.

Cooling after solidification was sufficiently slow to allow a high degree of B2 order for alloys rich in Al, and a good degree of DO3 order for alloys containing 25–30% Al (as indicated by strong superlattice spots and coarse DO3 domains in TEM).
Compression samples cut from the ingots by spark machining, either as 3 mm diameter or as 5 mm × 5 mm square cross-section samples, of height twice the diameter or width.

processing_steps.method: polishing on fine (1500 grade) abrasive paper
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Flat surfaces were polished on fine (1500 grade) abrasive paper before testing.

Compressed at room temperature to a strain of 2–3% at a nominal strain rate of 3×10⁻⁴ s⁻¹; compression axis always parallel to the cylinder axis of the cast samples. Tests showed a smooth onset of plasticity with no discrete yield points and slightly curved stress–strain behaviour.

Thin samples cut from the centre of the deformed samples perpendicular to the stress axis using a diamond saw; thin foils prepared by twin-jet electropolishing with a 25% nitric acid in methanol mixture at about 20 V and −30 °C.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Compression, axis parallel to the cylinder axis of the cast samples; tested to 2–3% strain.
measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: 3 mm diameter or 5 mm × 5 mm square cross-section, height twice the diameter or width

defects.type: superdislocations composed of 2×(1/2)111 partials; straight near-screw dislocations; edge dislocation dipoles and loops

microstructure_list.region: centre of the deformed compression sample (thin foil cut perpendicular to the stress axis)

defects.type: closely spaced parallel dislocation pairs, generally edge dipole segments and loops
straight screw superdislocations and paired dislocations formed by dislocation reactions giving stepped/jogged structures
broad residual-contrast fringes from APBII faults plus curved/kinked dislocation segments

structures.overall_structure: Polycrystalline, as-cast and slow-cooled Fe–30% Al + 0.1% B, weakly DO3-ordered (B2-derived long-range order). After room-temperature compression to 2–3% strain the deformation substructure consists of superdislocations composed of two (1/2)111 partials, predominantly straight and in near-screw orientations, together with many edge dislocation dipole segments and loops; dislocation reactions produce stepped structures and paired dislocations.

unmapped_findings: The TEM dislocation-structure study (Figs. 14–16) for the Fe–30% Al base is reported generically for that composition; the paper states that the ~0.1 at.% B addition caused only a slight increase in flow stress and no significant change in deformation/work-hardening behaviour, so the same substructure is assumed for the Fe–30% Al + 0.1% B sample.

Fe–30% Al (slow-cooled) is described as weakly DO3-ordered; a good degree of DO3 order is expected for alloys containing 25–30% Al, as indicated by strong superlattice spots and coarse DO3 domains in TEM. No evidence of coupled four-partial (perfect DO3) superdislocations was found for any material, including ~30% Al.

Compression tests on the as-cast slow-cooled samples showed a smooth onset of plasticity with no discrete yield points observed, and a slightly curved stress–strain behaviour with no sign of the linear stress–strain regions sometimes reported.

The peak in work hardening rate near 28–29% Al (over the 26–29% Al range) coincides with a maximum in elastic anisotropy (Zener factor A ≈ 6–7 at 28–30% Al); the paper attributes the tendency for dislocations to lie in screw orientations to strong Peierls forces near 25–30% Al rather than to the elastic anisotropy itself.
